status: completed relevance and independent occurrence-evidence review

review.requirement_proposition: Appropriate mechanisms should allow AI systems risking undue harm or exhibiting unwanted behaviour to be safely overridden, repaired or decommissioned as needed.
review.reason_for_change: The unwanted elevated errors in FedRAMP workspaces/API organisations engage the repair proposition. OpenAI's controlling notice reports all impacted services fully recovered on 26 June after investigation, with the mirrors corroborating the bounded interval. This is affirmative provider-reported evidence of repair for that service-restoration stage. It neither establishes continuous total downtime, underlying technical cause, all individual customer outcomes nor a certification/compliance-control breach.

conclusion_change.previous: OpenAI documented elevated errors in its FedRAMP service lane, investigated across several dated updates and reported recovery on 26 June. That supports a prolonged availability assessment, while the available notice does not identify a specific governance control, review artefact, decision or verification dependency that failed. The record remains unclassified under the current failure taxonomy because the prerequisites of the tested control-availability and evidence-access classes cannot be established from the FedRAMP label or duration alone. The affected functions and any customer-level governance consequence remain unresolved. Both clauses remain resolved-no-mapping. The FedRAMP designation and long duration establish neither breach of an identified authorization control nor failure of event capture, audit reconstruction or primary-evidence access. No specific admitted FedRAMP requirement is independently identified by the source’s service label. The fully adjudicated unclassified result and absence of external finding are bounded to the published function-level evidence gap.
